name: Pale Sea Grey
lede: Pale Sea Grey is a cool, slightly green grey that Ridgway's 1912 standards called Pale Dull Glaucous-Blue, a mouthful ColorHub's library flags itself as obscure.

sections.title: A plainer name for a Ridgway mouthful
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* records this exact swatch as Pale Dull Glaucous-Blue, on plate XLII, hue 41, tone f [1]. ColorHub's library tags that Ridgway name itself as an "obscure, qualified or novelty name," and files the color here under the plainer, more learnable Pale Sea Grey [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system, citing the same plate, classes it in block 184 [1]. *Glaucous* describes a dull, pale blue-green film, the kind that coats a plum's skin or a young eucalyptus leaf, which is closer to how the swatch actually reads than "sea" alone [1].

The nearest everyday name on file is [[ash]], about 5.5 units of ΔE away [1]. [[slate]], [[grey]] and [[powder-blue|Powder Blue]] sit in the same cool-neutral family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Pale Sea Grey in 254 of 23,781 paintings (1.07 percent), as photographed, almost entirely as a highlight [2]. It is markedly an Impressionist color here, over seven times the archive average, led by Alfred Sisley, Camille Pissarro and Eugène Boudin, all painters of coastal and river light [2]. It keeps company with Powder Blue and Sky Blue far more than chance, 61 and 22 times the base rate [2]. These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
